title: Simplify SmartRouter: deterministic fallback ordering and region routing cleanup
creator: Aisha Khatri
description: Problem: The current SmartRouter policy engine and regional routing code contain duplicated fallback logic and several undocumented ordering rules. This has led to surprising fallbacks during capacity pressure and an ongoing set of patches that are difficult to reason about. Aim: Consolidate policy evaluation into a single, testable engine, introduce a deterministic fallback ordering model (priority -> region affinity -> model family compatibility -> cost tier), and clean up region-specific routing code paths so rollouts and A/B experiments behave predictably. Scope: - Extract evaluator that produces an ordered list of candidate endpoints rather than returning a single endpoint inline. - Replace ad-hoc fallback heuristics in region routers with the evaluator output. - Remove duplicate compatibility mappings between model variants (server & client side) and centralize into the policy catalog. - Add unit and integration tests covering edge cases (partial capacity, multi-region failover, quantized model fallbacks). - Performance cleanup: reduce allocations in hot path, add a small LRU for short-lived request->route lookups, and inline a few hot functions in Go routing package. Out-of-scope: full rewrite of scheduler, pricing model changes.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic fallback ordering defined and codified in evaluator tests
No duplicated compatibility mappings in region router code (linter check)
Benchmark shows <10% p50 token latency regression and improved p95 under load compared to baseline after changes
Canary rollout plan with automated rollback conditions and observability dashboards
Documentation updated (CONFLUENCE link in notes) and a migration guide for Dedicated customers
notes: Proposed API change: evaluator returns ordered 'candids' list, router picks first satisfying runtime constraints
Implementation language: Go (service: router-service). Key packages: router/, policy/, catalog/
Risk: canary must cover region failover scenarios; fallback logic change could surface previously masked incompatibilities
Mitigation: add integration test jobs that run on every PR and a 48-hour canary with synthetic cross-region traffic
